body: Tunisian licence plates are black with white text. Military plates feature a small Tunisian flag on the left side.
In most coverage, the Google car is escorted by a follow car, which is a great way to recognize Tunisia.
The Google car in Tunisia is black with a medium-length, thin antenna.
Tunisia has Mediterranean, dry, and semi-desert climates.
Olive tree plantations with nicely arranged rows and raked, weedless soil are common.
Tunisia usually has white road lines, but some roads in Sfax have yellow middle lines.
Both French and Arabic are common, and you can often see bilingual signs.
Direction signs usually have a white background with towns listed in both Arabic and Latin script.
A traditional shade of blue is often used for doors, windows, and gates, especially on the island of Djerba.
Red and white striped curbs are common in Tunisia.
White concrete markers with a rounded red or yellow top show the distance to the nearest town and the road number.
Tunisia has a unique stop sign with both Arabic and Latin script.
A light green Toyota follow car is found only in the northernmost part of Tunisia.
The most common follow car is a dark green Mazda with a military license plate, found between Hammamet and Djerba.
Tunis has many different follow cars, including the light green Toyota.
The city of Kairouan has a unique white Mitsubishi follow car.
The island of Djerba is the only region where you are usually not accompanied by a follow car.
The area north of Tunis has a Mediterranean climate with hilly, agricultural terrain, often with fallow fields.
Between Tunis and Hammamet, the hills are higher and more vegetated.
Between Hammamet and Gabes, the landscape is flat and arid, with common olive tree plantations.
South of Gabes, the landscape becomes more desert-like. A distant mountain range may be visible to the southwest.
Djerba often features palm trees and whitewashed buildings with blue doors and windows.
Bizerte Lake is recognizable by its teal-colored water.
A large amount of palm trees in one place is a strong clue for Gabes.
Unique sandy hills can be found on the P1 road northwest of Medinine.
An off-road from P12 southwest of Sousse has dark pavement on bright sandy soil, with vegetation changing from prickly pears to arid.
The Djerba-Zarzis causeway is identifiable by water on both sides and a pipeline to the west.
Trekker coverage is available for various sites, including archaeological sites, forts, mosques, and a Star Wars set.
